bioRxiv search_preprints returned at most 30 results per page, not 100, so paging continued with cursor 30, 60, ... until a page came back empty or short.
PubMed get_article_metadata returns at most 20 articles per call, so each search was read in batches of 20.
No Figure 1 was reused: none of the three featured papers is open access (PubMed copyright status: all rights reserved or exclusive licence), so three illustrations were drawn by hand.
Revised preprints of older DOIs (2022-2025) whose DOI had never been posted were treated as new, per the README; their titles follow the latest version in the listing.
The 'Computational' tag was left off MPAQT and BEACON because the abstracts do not say whether new wet-lab data were generated.
No example posts or example reports were present in the data files, so nothing was deleted for that step.

notes: PubMed's get_copyright_status showed no CC BY or CC0 licence for any picked journal paper, and Figure 1 was not downloaded for any post, so all 21 posts use drawn illustrations. Three CC BY preprints (FlowMap, STAR Suite, IRES) could have used their own Figure 1.
Tier 1 [ta] searches match 'Nature' and 'Science' loosely (they also return Nat Ment Health and similar), so Tier 1 searches were narrowed by topic keywords to stay under PubMed's 20-operator limit.
The 10 journal-paper cap was reached by Tier 1 papers alone; several close Tier 2 papers (long-read replicate handling, APALORD, Dreamlet) were left out for that reason.

Unclear in the rules: whether revised old preprints (STAR Suite, IRES tools, first posted in March) count as new; they were posted because their DOIs were never posted before. Also unclear whether papers with chordoma as a minor part of a general spine series count as chordoma.
Journal authors are shown as first author et al. only. No chordoma preprints were found this week.
Quirk: the featured list was chosen as three Tier 1 cancer/RNA papers from the last 7 days.
